title: Cartwright Act: ban on use or distribution of common pricing algorithms (AB 325)
requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination or conspiracy to restrain trade, or to use or distribute one while coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or commercial term for the same or similar products or services in California. A 'common pricing algorithm' is any methodology, including software or other technology, used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set or otherwise influence a price or commercial term.
key_value: Unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (a) as part of a restraint-of-trade conspiracy, or (b) where the person coerces others to adopt its recommended price or commercial term
coverage_conditions: Applies to any person, other than the end consumer, who uses or distributes a common pricing algorithm for products or services in California. The law covers all industries, so it reaches residential rent-setting, but the statute does not name rentals. AB 325 also amends B&P Code § 16756.1 so that a Cartwright Act complaint need only plead facts making a contract, combination or conspiracy plausible, without excluding the possibility of independent action.
exemptions: By definition, it does not cover algorithms that are not used by two or more persons or that do not use competitor data, such as single-firm tools using only the business's own data.

interaction: Nothing in the section impairs or limits the applicability of antitrust laws.
penalty: Cartwright Act violations are punishable as a crime, per the Legislative Counsel's Digest; no specific penalty is stated in the bill text.

title: California statewide rent cap (Tenant Protection Act of 2019, AB 1482, as amended by SB 567)
requirement: Over any 12-month period, an owner of covered residential property may not raise the gross rental rate by more than 5% plus the change in the cost of living, or 10%, whichever is lower. The cap is measured from the lowest gross rental rate charged in the prior 12 months, with at most two increases in that period for the same tenant.
key_value: 5% + local CPI change, capped at 10%, whichever is lower; at most two increases per 12 months
coverage_conditions: Applies to residential real property (any dwelling or unit intended for human habitation, including units in a mobilehome park) unless exempt. Applies to rent increases on or after March 15, 2019 (mobilehome tenancies: on or after February 18, 2021). Does not apply to a homeowner of a mobilehome. Owners may set the initial rent for a new tenancy where no prior tenant remains in lawful possession.
exemptions: (1) Deed-restricted or government-agreement affordable housing for very low, low or moderate income households, or housing subject to an affordability subsidy agreement. (2) Dormitories owned and operated by a higher-education institution or a K-12 school. (3) Housing subject to a local rent or price control ordinance that limits annual increases to less than the state cap. (4) Housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (rolling), unless it is a mobilehome. (5) Residential property alienable separate from title to any other dwelling unit, such as single-family homes and condominiums, not owned by a REIT, a corporation, or an LLC with at least one corporate member, provided the tenant received the required written exemption notice (§ 1947.12(d)(5)). (6) A two-unit property where the owner occupies the other unit as a principal residence.
